programmes.d: The always virile Burt Reynolds reflects on his 1973 Cosmo poster, and his five-year romance with actress Loni Anderson. The maturing boy-toy-turned-movie-star is penning his autobiography.

Carol's guests are Diahann Carroll and Tim Conway for an episode that features two pairs of singles out on the town, and an Insomnia Theatre presentation of the romance movie "Arrivederci Summertime."
Brooke Shields discusses Sahara, Albert Brooks goes on a mild tirade and Johnny jokes about President Reagan.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Carol's guests tonight are Burt Reynolds and Nanette Fabray, who join the gang for a series of Carol's patented commercial parodies
The incomparable Sammy Davis, Jr. is tonight's guest. Sammy plays a flamboyant galley slave opposite Tim, then appears before the Queen (Carol) and King (Harvey) as a debt collector for a loan shark.
Actress Adrienne Barbeau worked as a secretary before landing on Broadway in Grease and then getting cast in TV hit Maude.
Tonight's sketches feature Harvey as a psychiatrist trying to unlock the secret of patient Carol's crying jags, and Carol as Stella Toddler, reporting a mugging and robbery by Tim to the police.
You'll really like Sally Field when she dishes on Burt Reynolds, and Buddy Hackett discusses desert islands with beautiful women and arguing with his wife. Also featured is Eubie Blake.
Oscar winner James Stewart (Philadelphia Story) chats about his holiday shopping and plans for Christmas. He talks about getting older and his new hearing aid.

programmes.t: Comedy Legends from The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Flip Wilson's "Old Man and the Church"; Jean Carroll's "Husband and New Apartment"; George Burns' "Stand-Up, Songs, and Nudity & Films"; Phil Silvers and Bing Crosby's "Comedy Mix-Up On Stage with Phil Silvers & Bing Crosby"
Whipped cream anyone? Burt Reynolds shows a clip of him squirting whipped cream down Johnny’s trousers. Burt then shoves a can in his own pants and sprays his crotch.

programmes.t: The Best of The Ed Sullivan Show
programmes.d: Ed Sullivan presents the Four Tops, Pearl Bailey, and Pat Boone.
This turbo-charged episode featured the comedy triumvirate of David Letterman, Chevy Chase, and Dan Aykroyd. So many jokes, so little time.
This time around Garry talks about turning 30, Chinese food, and...sex education.
Glenn Close discusses two movies that couldn't be more different--"Fatal Attractions" and "The Big Chill."
Arnold can't help but talk about his workout habits and Johnny jokes about killer bees. Ed Begley Jr. and Ginger McLamb also appear.

programmes.t: The Best of the Dean Martin Show
programmes.d: Sketches and songs with Dean Martin and celebrity guests Glen Campbell, Dom DeLuise, Kay Medford, and Gale Gordon.
Luke Skywalker, a.k.a. Mark Hamill, chats about the making of the iconic movie Star Wars and working with the legendary Alec Guiness.
Oscar nom’d George Segal demonstrates playing an old man using prosthetics, glasses and gait. Comedian Drew Carey riffs on his high school reunion, driving a Yugo and his love of bad food.
Buddy Ebsen and Wayne Rogers guest star! Sketches include: "The West Dakota County Fair", the World War II movie spoof, "War Is Heck", and another visit with "The Old Folks."
No one is safe when Don Rickles visits the set! But Cheryl Ladd and Ray Bradbury will make you feel right at home again.
Billy Crystal does impressions and sounds off on cable TV vs. satellite dishes, Arnold Schwarzenegger works out for an hour a day and Michael Ammar does card tricks with all of them.

John Byner and Petula Clark head downtown to the show. Along with classic characters ("The Old Folks" and Alice Portnoy), TV commercial spoofs and the firing of Donald Duck (Byner) are on tap tonight.

programmes.t: The Best of the Carol Burnett Show
programmes.d: Ms. Betty White is tonight's guest! Betty joins in the latest installment of 'The Family' wherein Mama has decided to clean up her attic.
TV's "The Odd Couple"--Jack Klugman and Tony Randall--guest star! Jack sings (!) with Carol, while Tony takes part in a sketch revealing superstitions among actors as part of a tribute to Broadway.
James Woods talks body casts, Peter Billingsley plans to quit acting when he turns 18 and Martin Mull takes an audience poll.
